summary: Returns the value as a range, or throws.
description: An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard reads the tag the object reports for itself: `value.toString() === "Range"`. A plain object that reports the same tag passes too, which in practice means a test double.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, typed as a range.

throws.InvalidRangeException: the value is not a range.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
const range = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveRange();

requireRange(range); // => range
requireRange({}); // throws InvalidRangeException
requireRange(null); // throws InvalidRangeException
```
